Next steps: if you can share the traffic sheet and a contact for procurement (for a short non-prod access addendum), we'll schedule the test kickoff early next week.

- Traffic envelope (attached): peak QPS during business hours ~ 1,100 QPS, sustained average ~ 320 QPS. Concurrent active chat sessions (web/mobile) ~ 1,800 with ~2,500 ephemeral websocket connections at peak.

- Measurement: ops@veridian.ai would prefer measurements from our edge so we capture real-world network effects; we can also expose an internal vantage if you want a fabric-only measurement.

Elena — great detail, thanks. A few clarifying tech asks and our proposed minimal test plan so expectations are aligned: 

- Vantage: We'll run tests measured from the client edge (as requested). Please confirm one or two public IP ranges or a short-lived endpoint we can hit for load testing.
- Concurrency shaping: For the streaming probe we need to reproduce ~2,000 concurrent websockets but at lower token rates initially — can you confirm typical tokens/sec per session? If you don't have that, we'll run a sweep (0.5, 1, 2 tokens/sec) to find the sensitivity.
- Request distribution: Short (<= 40 tokens) 50% / Medium (40–250 tokens) 35% / Long (>250 tokens) 15% — let us know if that matches your real mix.
- Measurement details we will capture: end-to-end request latency (first byte, last byte), token-level latency for streaming, and server-side tail traces (to map kernel/queuing vs network).

Proposed PoC test plan (short):
  Day 0: baseline runs (controlled QPS < 100) — collect traces
  Day 1–3: ramp to average QPS, run p95/p99 sweeps for hosted vs incumbent
  Day 4: streaming concurrency probe (incremental websocket connect up to 2k)
  Day 5–7: peak-day simulation (1,000–1,100 QPS) + final comparison report

I'll attach a one-pager test plan (redwood_test_plan_v1.pdf) to this thread. Once we have the sample queries and IPs, we'll schedule the kickoff.
